quote: In der Lobatschefskyschen Geometrie eine Gerade construiren, die zu 2 gegebenen parallel ist
english: In Lobachevskian geometry, to construct a line that is parallel to 2 given lines.
topic: The page argues that a Dedekind cut need not exist in a non-Archimedean number system, states that his geometries lead to non-Archimedean groups, and attempts a construction of a line parallel to two given lines in Lobachevskian geometry; that last section is crossed out.

triage.modern_statement: In the hyperbolic (Bolyai–Lobachevsky) plane, take two lines a and b. Construct a line that is asymptotically (limiting) parallel to both. Put another way: given one end (ideal point) of a and one end of b, show that a line with those two prescribed ends exists, and construct it, using only the plane axioms of incidence, order and congruence plus the hyperbolic parallel axiom, without continuity. This is a foundational construction problem in axiomatic hyperbolic geometry, not an open research question.
triage.answered_by: Hilbert himself. In 'Neue Begründung der Bolyai-Lobatschefskyschen Geometrie' (Mathematische Annalen 57, 1903, pp. 137–150; also reprinted as an appendix to later editions of Grundlagen der Geometrie), he proved that a line with any two prescribed ends exists. That result is the basis of his arithmetic of ends. The Annalen paper is the documented answer. A plausible but unconfirmed reading is that this crossed-out diary note was an early attempt at that lemma.

evidence.claim: Hilbert published 'Neue Begründung der Bolyai-Lobatschefskyschen Geometrie' in Mathematische Annalen vol. 57 (June 1903), pp. 137–150.

A chapter on Hilbert's end-calculus states that Hilbert first proved that two lines that neither meet nor are parallel have a common perpendicular, and then proved that a line with two prescribed ends exists. That is exactly a line parallel to two given lines.
Hilbert's arithmetic of ends makes the set of ends (ideal points) of a hyperbolic plane into a field. This rests on the existence of lines joining two ends.
Hilbert's hyperbolic parallel axiom, as formulated in the 1903 'Neue Begründung', is the framework for this work.

Later papers kept analysing Hilbert's 1903 foundations and which constructions are possible in the hyperbolic plane, for example 'Über die Hilbertsche Begründung der hyperbolischen Geometrie' and 'Ein Beitrag zur Konstruierbarkeit geometrischer Aufgaben in der hyperbolischen Ebene', both of which cite Hilbert 1903.

triage.why: The note states a concrete construction problem: a common asymptotic parallel to two lines, i.e. a line through one end of each. Hilbert solved it in his 1903 Annalen paper, where the existence of a line with two prescribed ends is a key lemma for the end-calculus. It is not one of the 23 problems or the 24th problem. Work on constructibility in Hilbert-style hyperbolic planes continued in foundations of geometry, but this specific problem is settled. Confidence is medium for three reasons. The diary page is undated. The line is crossed out. And I could not check the exact wording and section of the 1903 paper because the search budget ran out. The 'two prescribed ends' result is supported by a secondary source (the end-calculus chapter), not the original text.
